intel.t: Money out of politics, money in your pocket, Medicare for All, with lower living costs and wider health care access.

intel.l: Biggest vulnerability as opponents frame it
intel.t: Rogers calls Medicare for All outrageously expensive and says El-Sayed would defund police, which he denies; Jewish Democrats and Rogers attack his Israel and AIPAC rhetoric.
Black voters and independents: a Mitchell poll published October 5 had him at 71 to 9 among Black voters, 46 to 34 among independents and 45.6 to 41.4 overall, and up 50 to 33 among women.
Reports of up to $9 million moving from AIPAC's super PAC to a pro-Rogers group after the October 14 deadline.
PolitiFact rated his pharma lobbyist attack on Rogers Pants on Fire.

bottom: El-Sayed beat Rep. Haley Stevens by less than a point in the August 4 primary despite heavy AIPAC aligned spending against him. He then set a Michigan record with $30.7 million raised from July 16 to September 30, 2026, per Bridge Michigan, https://bridgemi.com/uncategorized/abdul-el-sayed-sets-michigan-fundraising-record-see-whos-contributing/. VoteLog shows $45,175,567 raised through September 30, $39,666,902 of it from individuals and only $364,721 from PACs, https://votelog.org/investigations/michigan-senate-general-money. He spends nearly all of it; cash was $3.8 million at September 30 against Rogers' $6.5 million.
Interests with money and a live decision:

**Pro-Israel groups, opposing.** UDP, AIPAC's super PAC, spent about $33 million in the primary against him and for Stevens, per AdImpact via Newsweek, and nearly $100,000 on general election mailers, https://www.newsweek.com/aipac-dumps-last-minute-9m-behind-mike-rogers-in-rebuke-of-abdul-el-sayed-12607752. Newsweek, relaying another outlet, says UDP is moving up to $9 million to a pro-Rogers super PAC. The lever is U.S. aid to Israel, which he criticizes.
**SMP and party.** WinSenate at $36,579,898 is the largest group on his side. The DSCC gave $62,000 on August 5, 2026.

intel.t: Lost manufacturing jobs, high utility and auto insurance costs, and support for ICE and photo ID; he calls El-Sayed's Medicare for All outrageously expensive.

intel.l: Biggest vulnerability as opponents frame it
intel.t: El-Sayed says he is in bed with big pharma, wealthy from trading on congressional relationships, and has a war for everything; the pharma lobbyist version of that attack was rated Pants on Fire.
Men, 51 to 40 in a Mitchell poll published October 5, 2026, with El-Sayed ahead 45.6 to 41.4 overall.
He launched Democrats for Mike Rogers in Detroit on August 20 to court Democrats uneasy with El-Sayed, including Jewish Democrats.
Reports that AIPAC's super PAC is moving up to $9 million to a pro-Rogers group after the October 14 deadline.
He ran about 123,000 votes behind Trump in Michigan in 2024.

bottom: Rogers lost to Elissa Slotkin in 2024 by just over 19,000 votes, https://bridgemi.com/michigan-government/mike-rogers-vs-abdul-el-sayed-7-issues-defining-michigans-us-senate-race/. This time he trails El-Sayed in hard dollars but leads in cash and outside support. VoteLog shows $20,565,706 raised and $6,527,471 cash through September 30, 2026, and $132,512,494 in outside money benefiting him against $69,975,072 for El-Sayed, https://votelog.org/investigations/michigan-senate-general-money.
Interests with money and a live decision:
**Party and Trump world.** SLF at $40,657,615 and No Going Back PAC at $32,709,224 lead his outside side. SLF pledged more than $45 million in April.

**Pro-Israel.** NORPAC and RJC PAC gave directly, and Newsweek, relaying another outlet, says AIPAC's UDP is moving up to $9 million into Great Lakes Conservatives Fund after the October 14 disclosure deadline, https://www.newsweek.com/aipac-dumps-last-minute-9m-behind-mike-rogers-in-rebuke-of-abdul-el-sayed-12607752.

D.t: Abdul El-Sayed leads by 4.8 in the forecast and wins 83% of simulations. The cushion is about 239,353 votes; a one point swing is about 24,778 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +1.7 and D +11.5. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is D +4.4. Your best recent poll is Cygnal (R)/Beacon Research (D) at D +6.5; your worst is Marist University at R +0.2. 23 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Wayne, a projected net 296,556 votes; Oakland, a projected net 112,275 votes; Washtenaw, a projected net 97,369 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Macomb, R +1.8, 8.7% of the vote; Kent, D +3.9, 6.7% of the vote; Saginaw, D +0.6, 1.8% of the vote; Muskegon, D +2.5, 1.7% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Abdul El-Sayed runs furthest behind in Ottawa, Berrien, Kent. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 79% of voters, 43 to 54, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.93 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 74% of voters, 51 to 46, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.72 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 60% of voters, 57 to 39, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.98 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Abdul El-Sayed: Immigration voters 19 to 78, Small counties 34 to 63, Voters who can afford daily costs 42 to 54. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$2.6M cash against $6.5M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.4 points toward Abdul El-Sayed. Bank it: chase the remaining mail ballots and low propensity voters who have not voted.
Activity: 5 campaign stops by the candidate or surrogates in 30 days.
El-Sayed says he is in bed with big pharma, wealthy from trading on congressional relationships, and has a war for everything; the pharma lobbyist version of that attack was rated Pants on Fire.

In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +11.5 and R +1.7. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is D +4.4. Your best recent poll is Marist University at R +0.2; your worst is Cygnal (R)/Beacon Research (D) at D +6.5. 23 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Ottawa, a projected net 37,256 votes; Livingston, a projected net 21,853 votes; St. Clair, a projected net 19,712 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Macomb, R +1.8, 8.7% of the vote; Kent, D +3.9, 6.7% of the vote; Saginaw, D +0.6, 1.8% of the vote; Muskegon, D +2.5, 1.7% of the vote.

R.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Mike Rogers runs furthest behind in Macomb, Wayne, St. Clair. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 79% of voters, 54 to 43, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.93 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 74% of voters, 46 to 51, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.72 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 60% of voters, 39 to 57, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.98 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Mike Rogers: Black voters 11 to 86, Asian and other voters 24 to 72, Health care and Social Security voters 28 to 69. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$6.5M cash against $2.6M. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.

media.what: Said he would not vote for Republican Mike Rogers and praised Democrat Abdul El-Sayed's campaign, in a conversation with Saagar Enjeti.
In his newsletter, defended El-Sayed's 2021 remarks on post 9/11 U.S. military action after the Rogers campaign attacked them.
Endorsed and campaigned with El-Sayed; in September the El-Sayed campaign publicly disagreed with remarks Piker made in an Axios interview.
As a guest on The Tucker Carlson Show he praised El-Sayed's populist message and predicted he would likely beat Mike Rogers.
Argued El-Sayed is doing well because of his hard line on Israel and domestic focus, and called Republican Mike Rogers a 'neocon' whose attacks will not energize the GOP base.
Interviewed Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed on The Weekly Show about his closing argument to skeptical Michigan voters.
Responded to Abdul El-Sayed's vow to beat him in a debate by saying he would have El-Sayed on and that his criticism of Islam is about ideas, not people.
Interviewed Abdul El-Sayed on Noosphere, where El-Sayed said he would go on Bill Maher's show and win the debate.
Sabato's Crystal Ball moved the Michigan Senate race from Toss-up to Leans Democratic.
Named Oakland County as the key area to watch in the El-Sayed versus Rogers race.
Called Abdul El-Sayed 'weird' and obsessed with sex over his comments about JD Vance's children and mocked his posture.
Ran a segment on El-Sayed's campaign and the GOP strategy in Michigan under the line that the only poll that matters is on Election Day.
